audit_findings.title: Consolidated owner-earnings adjustments may belong partly to noncontrolling investors
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable net income is combined with consolidated D&A, capital spending and other OE adjustments, affecting the historical OE series and $640.6 million anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Earnings, tax attributes and cash flows are allocated to both NIPSCO and the tax equity partner in varying percentages by category and over the life of the partnership.
audit_findings.explanation: The inconsistent ownership basis is a demonstrated methodological error. Its net valuation effect is unresolved because consolidated D&A add-backs tend to overstate parent OE, consolidated capital deductions can understate it, and tax-equity waterfalls do not follow fixed ownership percentages. The record cannot establish the net correction or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild each historical OE adjustment from actual NiSource distribution rights across the 19.9% NIPSCO interest, 19.9% GenCo interest and each tax-equity waterfall, then recompute the trend anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may require dilution absent from the static denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth-related interest expense reduces future equity OE, while future common issuance increases the per-share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: In order to finance the construction of the Contract Assets, as well as any generation and transmission assets we develop to support future data center contracts, we expect to incur significant additional long-term debt and issue additional equity in NiSource, in addition to the financing we otherwise would seek to support investments in our existing businesses and refinance existing indebtedness.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that additional debt and NiSource equity will be required, but it does not quantify the future shares or identify how much of the model's 3% and 5% growth depends on financed data-center investment. The static 489.9565 million-share denominator therefore presents a real omission whose materiality cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Map each scenario's growth to required projects and produce annual debt, interest, Blackstone contribution and NiSource share-issuance schedules before recalculating per-share value.

audit_findings.title: A null perimeter does not capture the new $7 billion ADS undertaking
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $7.0 billion of filed Contract Assets, equal to 77.2% of the $9.07 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The undertaking changes the operating perimeter, future OE, growth capital, financing costs, minority claims and share count.
audit_findings.evidence: The aggregate cost of the Generation Assets, together with the cost to develop related transmission infrastructure (collectively, the “Contract Assets”), is currently estimated to be approximately $7 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter omission. The project is comparable in scale to the entire calculated equity value and was approved and under development by the valuation date. It can add positive project economics, but it can also reduce value through financing, dilution, construction penalties, capped reimbursement and the 19.9% outside claim. Either direction is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Add a separate ADS/GenCo valuation module using approved contractual terms, construction timing, capital contributions, debt and equity financing, operating cash flows, liquidated damages, termination caps and the capacity-reduction option; then consolidate only NiSource-attributable value.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized financing costs may bypass the retained-interest rail
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $70.5 million pre-tax in 2025 ($32.7 million AFUDC equity plus $37.8 million borrowed-funds allowance and capitalized interest), equal to 11.0% of the $640.6 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Unreversed AFUDC equity inflates OE with noncash income, while capitalized interest omits financing cost from equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For rate-regulated companies where provided for in rates, AFUDC is capitalized on all classes of property except organization costs, land, autos, office equipment, tools and other general property purchases.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether these amounts were omitted is unresolved, not demonstrated. Even treating the full $70.5 million as an OE overstatement would only lower an already discounted valuation: the bull value is $20.66 versus the $41.39 market price. The issue cannot reverse the valuation conclusion, although it should be corrected for accuracy.
audit_findings.action: Trace every year's AFUDC-equity and capitalized-interest entries through the OE worksheet and rerun the anchor if either item was not reversed consistently.

audit_findings.title: Recurring retirement and remediation cash may be missing from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $261.3 million of identified 2025 gross cash outflows ($73.0 million of ARO payments plus $188.3 million of cost of removal), equal to 40.8% of the $640.6 million anchor before recoveries or double-counting
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncaptured settlements and removal expenditures reduce recurring distributable cash and therefore the OE anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: We accrue for costs associated with environmental remediation obligations, including expenditures related to asset retirement obligations and cost of removal, when the incurrence of such costs is probable and the amounts can be reasonably estimated, regardless of when the expenditures are actually made.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates large recurring cash outflows, but it does not establish that the OE calculation omitted them or how much was contemporaneously recovered from customers or already included in maintenance capital. The possible correction is nevertheless large enough relative to anchor OE to be material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile ARO settlements, environmental remediation and cost-of-removal cash by year to maintenance capital and regulatory cash recoveries; deduct only the unrecovered, non-duplicated recurring amount and rerun the OE series.

audit_findings.title: Regulatory-asset recovery is a large untested earnings assumption
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,499.4 million of regulatory assets at 2025 year-end, including $499.3 million not earning a return
audit_findings.mechanism: Disallowance would reduce future OE, while delayed or non-return-bearing recovery would reduce growth and the present value of cash receipts.
audit_findings.evidence: If we determine that the amounts included as regulatory assets are no longer probable of recovery, a charge to income would immediately be required to the extent of the unrecoverable amounts.
audit_findings.explanation: No filed disallowance or impairment is presently demonstrated; management continued to consider recovery probable. This is therefore a forward-looking regulatory risk rather than a current numerical error, although the exposed balances are large and adverse rulings could materially reduce value.
audit_findings.action: Monitor regulatory orders and recovery schedules by asset category, and run disallowance and delayed-recovery sensitivities for retired coal, safety, depreciation and data-center-related balances when case-specific evidence becomes available.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum supplied residual of $137.6 million in 2024, equal to 21.5% of the $640.6 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any qualifying residual D&A would be added to historical OE and could raise the trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2018 $31.1m (5.2% of filed D&A); FY2019 $37.1m (5.2% of filed D&A); FY2021 $26.9m (3.6% of filed D&A); FY2022 $82.7m (10.1% of filed D&A); FY2023 $73.8m (8.1% of filed D&A); FY2024 $137.6m (13.2% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative rather than an overstatement. As an intentionally extreme scale test, adding the entire $137.6 million residual as recurring anchor OE would raise the bull value only to approximately $25.06 per share, still 39.5% below the $41.39 market price. The actual eligible portion must be smaller or equal, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from filed asset and amortization schedules and rerun only for components demonstrated to be eligible non-economic add-backs.
